title: nvsh bash hook + agent on error

targets.text: nvsh elevates your existing bash into a self-healing NVIDIA shell: install one sourced hook, keep bash exactly as it is, and when a command fails an NVIDIA-opinionated agent (Pi.dev driving the local associate model by default) appears inline with a diagnosis and a proposed fix you approve, retry and verify; /ask, /fix, /doctor and Ctrl+G reach the same agent on demand, and successful commands never pay a millisecond for it.

On spark, thor and orin, 'nvsh setup' then a normal session shows no visible change on successful commands, and 'ls /nope' produces the inline panel with the real 'No such file or directory' text in its context (--show-context).

Zero cost on the success path: the sourced bash hook is a pure-bash function that reads $? and PIPESTATUS, applies the cheap trigger pre-filter (0, 130, 141, empty line, leading-space/ignored history) in bash, and only execs the Python entrypoint when a failure qualifies. Measured on this Spark: the uv-tool entrypoint costs ~45 ms (associate --help 0.051 s, nvsh --help 0.043 s), which is too much to pay on every prompt but fine on a failure.
Sourcing the hook and running 1000 successful commands in 'bash --norc -i' forks no nvsh process (strace -f -e execve count of nvsh == 0) and adds < 5 ms median to prompt latency.

Trigger rules are a table-tested pure-Python module (nvsh/triggers.py) consulted by the entrypoint before any agent call: 130, 141, grep/diff exit 1, false, test/[ ], commands run inside scripts, pipelines without pipefail (PIPESTATUS is passed in by the hook), interactive/long-running programs, plus a rate limit. Pattern triggers for exit-0 failures are opt-in.
tests/test_triggers.py is table-driven over (command, exit, PIPESTATUS, interactive-program flag, rate state) and covers every rule in CLAUDE.md's trigger list; all non-error rows produce 'no call'.

Slash commands (/ask /fix /explain /retry /doctor /context /agent /help) are routed inside the same bash session by binding Enter (C-m) to a readline macro that first runs a bind -x function then accept-line (C-j). The function inspects READLINE_LINE: a line whose first word is a registered slash command is rewritten to a hidden `nvsh slash <line>` call prefixed with one space (so HISTCONTROL ignorespace keeps it out of history) and the original line is pushed with 'history -s'. Unregistered '/foo', absolute paths, quoted multi-line input and plain commands pass through unchanged. Verified in a throwaway bash 5.2 under script(1) on the Spark: /doctor and '/ask why is memory high?' routed, /notacmd and 'ls -d /tmp' ran as bash, a quoted two-line echo (Enter inside the quotes) continued normally. command_not_found_handle does NOT fire for '/doctor', so this rebind is required.

In an interactive Ghostty session on the Spark with Ghostty's own integration loaded: /doctor routes, 'history' shows '/doctor' and not the dispatch line, '/tmp/x' runs as a path, a quoted two-line echo (Enter pressed inside the quotes) continues, and no visible flicker or duplicated prompt appears.

Completion: 'complete -I -F' (bash >= 5 initial-word completion) supplies the '/'+Tab palette: for a first word starting with '/' and containing no second '/', it merges registered slash commands with compgen -f path matches, so '/'+Tab lists /ask /doctor ... next to /etc /tmp, '/do'+Tab completes to /doctor, '/tm'+Tab still completes /tmp/, and every other word falls through via compopt -o bashdefault -o default ('ec'+Tab still lists echo). `complete -F <fn> /doctor` supplies per-command argument completion ('/doctor '+Tab lists gpu docker cuda memory services). Verified on the Spark in a throwaway bash 5.2 with bash-completion 2.11 loaded. fzf and ble.sh stay optional.
'/'+Tab, '/do'+Tab, '/doctor '+Tab, '/tm'+Tab and 'ec'+Tab behave as in scope entry s18 in a real Ghostty session and over ssh to orin (no bash-completion assumptions beyond the stock package).

Agent boundary: nvsh/agent/ defines a small NvshAgent contract (request kinds failure|slash|explicit, streamed events text-delta|tool-call|proposal|status|done|error, cancel, capabilities) with a FakeAgent for tests and PiAgent as the default. PiAgent spawns 'pi --mode rpc' (pi 0.84.2 installed, JSONL over stdio with prompt/abort/get_state/switch_session commands and message_update/tool_execution_* events, documented in the shipped docs/rpc.md) as one long-lived subprocess per shell session so a failure does not pay pi's ~0.35 s node startup each time.

nvsh/agent/ imports nothing from pi; FakeAgent drives the full failure -> proposal -> approve -> retry -> verify loop in tests without pi installed; PiAgent's rpc reader splits on LF only and handles abort and a killed pi process without hanging the shell.

Deterministic nvsh tools (inspect_gpu, inspect_memory, inspect_containers, inspect_services, read_logs, retry_command, verify) are implemented once in Python. To expose them to Pi as first-class tools, nvsh ships one generic TypeScript extension file loaded via `pi -e <path>` that forwards each call to `nvsh tool <name> --json`; pi has no RPC command to register tools from outside the process (verified in docs/extensions.md and docs/rpc.md). Mutating proposals surface as 'proposal' events and are confirmed by the operator in nvsh, mirroring shell-cli's operations.py apply=False default and deny-wins policy. (Per decision c25, v1 uses only pi's bash tool; the extension shim is the later migration path.)

No agent-proposed command ever runs without an explicit operator keypress; the audit log records every proposal, the decision and the outcome; the fixture test asserts a 'sudo rm -rf' proposal is shown but never executed.

Default model: nvsh's config ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/nvsh/config.toml: [agent] provider=pi, [agents.pi] provider=nemotron model=associate) names Pi's own provider/model; the endpoint (a lobes-gateway at 192.168.1.138:8000, NOT this machine, which is 192.168.1.157) and its bearer key stay in ~/.pi/agent/models.json. nvsh never stores or forwards keys, and 'nvsh doctor' reports whether pi is on PATH and whether the configured provider answers /v1/models (both endpoints answered 'invalid_api_key' unauthenticated, so reachability is a 401-vs-timeout check).

$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/nvsh/config.toml (stdlib tomllib) selects the harness and pi provider/model; grep of the nvsh package and tracked files finds no API key and no non-localhost endpoint; 'nvsh doctor' distinguishes pi-missing, endpoint-unreachable and endpoint-401 with distinct remediations.

Platform detection is file-first and reports its sources: /etc/dgx-release (DGX_NAME, DGX_SWBUILD_VERSION, OTA version), /etc/nv_tegra_release (Jetson, absent here), /proc/device-tree/model, /sys/class/dmi/id/product_name (NVIDIA_DGX_Spark), /usr/local/cuda/version.json (13.0.2), /proc/driver/nvidia/version (580.126.09), /proc/meminfo. On GB10 nvidia-smi reports memory.total/used as [N/A] (verified), so the CUDA-OOM signal is MemAvailable and dmesg OOM-killer, not VRAM. When dgx-spark-cli's 'spark status --json' is installed nvsh calls it; cuDNN, TensorRT and nvpmodel are absent on this Spark and must be reported as absent, not guessed. All of this is recorded in docs/platforms.md.

'nvsh context --show' on the Spark reports DGX Spark / DGX OS 7.x / CUDA 13.0.2 / driver 580.126.09 / unified memory with MemAvailable, each with its source path, and reports cuDNN, TensorRT and nvpmodel as absent rather than omitting them; docs/platforms.md lists every source with the verifying command.

Context collector + redactor: bounded command line, exit code, PIPESTATUS, cwd, captured output when available, platform block; redaction of HF_TOKEN=, --api-key, Authorization:, .env-style assignments runs before anything leaves the process, with its own tests and --show-context. The operator's ~/.bashrc exports many plaintext tokens, so the collector never sources or dumps rc files.

tests/test_redact.py scrubs HF_TOKEN=, --api-key, Authorization: Bearer, OPENAI_API_KEY=, .env-style KEY=value lines and ssh private-key blocks from the corpus, and asserts the redactor runs before PiAgent.run receives the context; --show-context prints exactly the bytes that would be sent.

Packaging: pyproject's hatch wheel config lists only packages=['nvsh'] with no artifacts/force-include, so the bash integration must be either a Python string rendered by 'nvsh install bash' or an explicit include; the runtime stays dependencies=[] (stdlib subprocess/json/select). New verbs (install, uninstall, hook, run, ask, fix, explain-last, complete, tool, agent) follow the register(sub)/CliError/emit_result/--json contract and each gets a catalog entry so teken cli doctor --strict stays green.

Building the wheel and installing it in a clean venv gives a working 'nvsh setup' that writes the bash integration file; 'uv run teken cli doctor . --strict' and the full lint set pass; dependencies stays [].

Docs and prompts: add docs/architecture.md (hook decision and why, issue #1 milestone 1) and docs/platforms.md; update README's planned-verbs section and 'what leaves the machine'; rewrite the login-shell sections of CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.colleague.md, QWEN.md and .pi/SYSTEM.md so all four harness prompts describe the hook architecture; bump the version.

docs/architecture.md records hook-over-wrap with the reasons and the parked login-shell mode; all four harness prompt files describe the same architecture; scripts/harness-smoke.py --stage config passes; the version is bumped.

Jetson detection sources verified on real hardware over ssh (thor = AGX Thor devkit, orin = AGX Orin devkit): /etc/nv_tegra_release first line (thor 'R38 (release), REVISION: 2.2', orin 'R39 (release), REVISION: 2.0'), /proc/device-tree/model ('NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor Developer Kit' / 'NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin Developer Kit'), /proc/device-tree/compatible (tegra264 / tegra234), dpkg nvidia-l4t-core (orin 39.2.0) or nvidia-cuda 7.0-b128 (thor), /usr/include/aarch64-linux-gnu/cudnn_version.h, libnvinfer10 dpkg, nvidia-smi name 'NVIDIA Thor' / 'Orin (nvgpu)' with memory [N/A] like GB10, nvpmodel -q ('NV Power Mode: MAXN 0'), tegrastats one-sample RAM line, /etc/docker/daemon.json default-runtime (nvidia on thor, unset on orin). Orin has no /usr/local/cuda/version.json and no tensorrt python module, so every source must be optional and reported as absent when missing.

'nvsh context --show' over ssh on thor reports L4T R38.2 / AGX Thor / CUDA 13 / cuDNN 9.12 / TensorRT 10.13 / nvpmodel MAXN, and on orin reports L4T R39.2 / AGX Orin and marks the CUDA toolkit and TensorRT as absent.

Jetson runtime floor: thor and orin both run bash 5.2.21 and Python 3.12.3, have 'script' and ssh, but neither has pi, fzf or a user PROMPT_COMMAND; orin also lacks uv and tmux, and thor's uv is a snap. The bash hook and the Python entrypoint must work there with only the system Python 3.12 and no pi on PATH: doctor reports 'pi not installed' with the install remediation, and the agent degrades to a stdlib OpenAI-compatible adapter (associate's harness/pi.py:831-863 urllib pattern) pointed at a configured endpoint rather than failing.

On orin with only system Python 3.12 and no pi, uv or tmux: the hook installs, a failure shows the panel with 'pi not installed' and the install/other-harness offer, and the stdlib adapter works when pointed at a configured endpoint.

No third-party runtime dependencies (pyproject dependencies=[] stays); pi is an external optional binary, never a Python dependency, and absence of pi, tmux, fzf, spark (dgx-spark-cli) or any NVIDIA tool degrades a feature, never breaks the shell.

pyproject dependencies == [] and 'python -X importtime -c "import nvsh.cli"' shows only stdlib modules; removing pi, tmux, fzf and spark from PATH leaves every shell command working and only degrades nvsh features with a diagnostic.

Untouched: culture.yaml (backend stays claude, never rewritten by code), .claude/skills (vendored verbatim from guildmaster), the .pi/skills relative symlink and the no-.pi/settings.json rule enforced by tests/test_pi_settings.py, and doctor's _PROMPT_FILE table which tests/test_harness_registries.py pins to backend-fingerprints.yaml.
git diff on culture.yaml, .claude/skills, .pi/skills and doctor._PROMPT_FILE is empty across the whole change; tests/test_pi_settings.py and tests/test_harness_registries.py still pass.

No endpoint or key lands in tracked JSON: scripts/scan-secrets.py fails CI on any non-localhost http URL under baseUrl/endpoint/url/host keys in JSON files, so config examples use localhost placeholders and the real provider mapping lives only in ~/.pi/agent/models.json on the machine.
scripts/scan-secrets.py passes; any example config under docs/ or nvsh/ uses http://localhost placeholders only.

Harness chooser: 'nvsh install' / 'nvsh agent use' detects which harness CLIs are on PATH (pi, qwen, claude, codex), defaults to pi, offers to install pi when absent (npm via nvm on the Spark; the Jetsons have no node today), or lets the operator pick another. Each harness is an NvshAgent adapter that drives the CLI's headless mode (pi --mode rpc; claude -p --output-format stream-json; codex exec --json; qwen -p) and reports its capabilities.

'nvsh agent list' shows pi, qwen, claude, codex with installed/not-installed status; with none installed the failure panel offers to install pi or pick another; each adapter passes the shared conformance test (stream, cancel, error, capability report).

Compose with Ghostty's bash integration, which is already active on the Spark (TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty 1.3.1, /usr/share/ghostty/shell-integration/bash/ghostty.bash): it appends __ghostty_hook to PROMPT_COMMAND array-aware and idempotently (ghostty.bash:295-308), uses PS0 for preexec on bash>=5.2 and otherwise sources bash-preexec.sh (line 312). nvsh's hook uses the same append pattern, registers through preexec_functions when bash-preexec is loaded instead of installing its own DEBUG trap, and preserves Ghostty's OSC 133 markers around its inline panel.

In Ghostty on the Spark, after 'nvsh setup', 'declare -p PROMPT_COMMAND' shows both __ghostty_hook and the nvsh hook exactly once each; 'trap -p DEBUG' shows no nvsh trap; Ghostty jump-to-prompt still works across an nvsh panel.

Session log hygiene: the typescript lives under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nvsh/ (tmpfs) with mode 0600, is rotated/truncated per session, only the slice for the failed command is read, redaction runs on that slice before it reaches any agent, and 'nvsh setup' explains the log exists. If script(1) or the log fails, the hook silently continues without capture.
The session log is mode 0600 under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nvsh/, is removed at shell exit, and a test proves only the last C..D slice is read; killing script(1) mid-session leaves the shell usable.

Operators (starting with Ori) who live at a bash prompt on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin/Thor and DGX Spark machines, locally in Ghostty and over ssh, and who want an NVIDIA engineer to appear only when something breaks.
README's opening names Jetson AGX Orin/Thor, DGX Spark, bash, Ghostty and ssh as the setting, and the install/uninstall checklist is executed on spark, thor and orin by the operator.

Today a failure on a Jetson or Spark means copying the error into a chat, re-deriving the machine's JetPack/CUDA/unified-memory facts by hand, and typing fixes back; nvsh itself is a scaffold with no shell behaviour (README.md:10-14) and its prompts still describe a PTY wrapper.
docs/architecture.md opens with this before-state and cites README.md:10-14 and the retired PTY-wrapper wording in the prompt files as of version 0.9.1.

After 'nvsh setup', the operator's own bash is unchanged on success; a qualifying failure shows an inline ⚡ nvsh panel within a second with a diagnosis built from the real output slice and the machine's detected facts, offers a proposed fix that runs only after Enter, retries, and reports whether it worked; /ask, /fix, /doctor, /explain, /retry and Ctrl+G reach the same warm pi session; 'nvsh uninstall' removes everything.

Two recorded demos exist in docs/: a CUDA-OOM-style failure in Ghostty on the Spark and a missing-package failure over ssh on orin, each showing panel, approve, retry and verify, plus 'nvsh uninstall' leaving PROMPT_COMMAND and ~/.bashrc as before.

The value is NVIDIA-specific and local: unified memory on GB10/Jetson, L4T/JetPack version skew, container runtime and power mode are what a generic 'explain my error' tool gets wrong, and the machines are often air-gapped, so the agent must run against a local model with the facts collected on-box.

The system prompt sent to the agent contains the detected platform block (unified memory, L4T/JetPack or DGX OS version, container runtime, power mode) and a test proves an air-gapped run (no network) still reaches a localhost model endpoint.

Measured: a successful command adds < 5 ms to the next prompt (bash-only hook, no fork); the panel's first agent text appears < 2 s after a qualifying failure on the Spark with a warm pi session; 0 agent calls for exit codes 130/141, grep/diff 1, false and test in the trigger table tests; 100% of the redaction test corpus is scrubbed; the hook installs and uninstalls cleanly on spark, thor and orin (3/3).

Each number is produced by a named test or checklist: tests/test_triggers.py (0 calls), tests/test_redact.py (100%), a timing test under script(1) (< 5 ms, < 2 s), and the 3-machine checklist in docs/ with dates.

Hook ordering and status capture: the nvsh hook is inserted as the FIRST element of the PROMPT_COMMAND array and captures $? and PIPESTATUS in its first statement; later elements (Ghostty's __ghostty_hook, others) run after it. Probe on the Spark: a hook placed after __ghostty_hook saw PIPESTATUS clobbered, while a first-position hook saw 'false | true' as '1 0' and 'true | false | true' as '0 1 0'; with the user's own 'set -o pipefail' the hook's $? becomes the pipeline status, which the trigger table must respect rather than override.

With Ghostty's integration loaded, 'declare -p PROMPT_COMMAND' lists the nvsh hook first; a test sources the hook, runs 'false | true' and 'true | false | true', and the hook records PIPESTATUS '1 0' and '0 1 0'; under 'set -o pipefail' the recorded status is 1.

Placement of the capture wrapper in ~/.bashrc: the exec into script(1) must be the first line after the distro's interactive guard ('If not running interactively' at line 40 on spark, 29 on thor, 28 on orin), guarded by an NVSH_WRAPPED env var, not appended at the end. Otherwise the whole rc (nvm, cargo, kiro-cli, bash-completion) runs twice and every new terminal pays a second 'bash -ic true' (0.25 s measured) before the prompt. 'nvsh setup' edits the rc idempotently inside a marked block and keeps a timestamped backup.

After 'nvsh setup', the exec line sits immediately after the interactive guard inside a marked block; 'bash -ic true' timing is within 10% of the pre-setup baseline; running setup twice leaves ~/.bashrc unchanged; a backup file exists.

Terminal portability: thor has no xterm-ghostty terminfo (infocmp fails), so an ssh from Ghostty arrives with TERM=xterm-ghostty and tput/clear break. The panel renders with hard-coded SGR sequences guarded by NO_COLOR / TERM=dumb / non-tty checks and never calls tput; 'nvsh doctor' detects missing terminfo and prints the 'infocmp -x | ssh host tic -x -' remediation.
In a shell with TERM=dumb and one with TERM=xterm-ghostty and no terminfo, the panel prints readable text without tput errors; doctor reports the missing terminfo with the tic remediation on thor.

Readline keymaps: the Enter macro, Ctrl+G and the palette are bound in the emacs, vi-insert and vi-command keymaps (one 'bind -m' per keymap); probe on the Spark showed a plain 'bind -x' binding does not fire after 'set -o vi' while a vi-insert keymap binding does.
In 'set -o vi' and in emacs mode, /doctor + Enter routes, Ctrl+G fires and '/'+Tab lists the palette (test drives both keymaps under script(1)).

pi launch hygiene: PiAgent starts pi with --no-context-files (otherwise pi reads CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md from the user's cwd into the prompt), --no-extensions, --no-skills, --no-prompt-templates, --no-approve, and either --no-session or --session-dir under $XDG_STATE_HOME/nvsh (0700). Probe: pi stores sessions per cwd under ~/.pi/agent/sessions (26 project dirs on the Spark), so an unflagged run would persist redacted-but-sensitive failure context into project-named session files.

The PiAgent argv is asserted in a test to contain --no-context-files --no-extensions --no-skills --no-prompt-templates --no-approve and a session flag; after a failure run, no new file appears under ~/.pi/agent/sessions.

Warm-session ownership: the long-lived pi process is owned by an nvsh session daemon started lazily on the first qualifying failure (never at shell start), listening on a per-user socket under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nvsh/; the 45 ms hook client connects, streams the panel, and exits. The daemon dies on an idle timeout and when its last shell exits (EXIT trap sends a stop); stale sockets are reaped at the next start. If the daemon or pi is missing or crashed, the client falls back to a one-shot 'pi -p' run so a failure is never left without a diagnosis.

Starting a shell creates no nvsh or pi process; the first qualifying failure starts one daemon; closing the shell leaves no nvsh or pi process behind (pgrep); with pi absent the client still produces a diagnosis or a clear 'no agent' panel within 2 s.

Upgrade path: the sourced ~/.local/share/nvsh/bash.sh carries the nvsh version that rendered it; the failure-path client compares it with its own version and prints 'run nvsh setup to refresh the hook' once per session when they differ. 'nvsh setup' is idempotent and re-renders; a 'uv tool upgrade nvsh' alone never breaks the shell because the old hook only calls stable verbs.
With the hook file stamped as an older version, the next failure prints the refresh notice once; 'nvsh setup' re-renders and the notice stops.

Kill switch and reversibility: NVSH_DISABLE=1 in the environment makes the sourced file a no-op; 'nvsh off' / 'nvsh on' unbind and rebind Enter, the palette and the hook in the current shell; 'nvsh uninstall' removes the marked block from ~/.bashrc (restoring from its backup if the block was edited), the hook file, runtime sockets and logs, and stops daemons. Hook functions never use set -e and end with '|| return 0'. Probe on the Spark: an erroring bind -x function still lets the Enter macro accept the line, so a bug degrades, it does not lock the terminal.

NVSH_DISABLE=1 bash -i shows no hook, no Enter macro (bind -p) and no capture; 'nvsh off' then '/doctor' runs as a path again; 'nvsh uninstall' restores ~/.bashrc byte-identical to the backup and leaves no files, sockets or processes.

Interrupt and cleanup: Ctrl+C while the panel is streaming sends rpc abort to pi, restores the terminal and returns to a clean prompt with the original failure still available to /fix; killing script(1) or the daemon mid-session leaves the shell usable; stale session logs under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nvsh are removed at next setup or shell start.

Ctrl+C during a streaming panel returns to a working prompt within 1 s, pi's get_state shows isStreaming false, and '/fix' still finds the last failure; kill -9 of script(1) or the daemon leaves the shell accepting commands.

The output slice sent to the agent is bounded (last 64 KB of the failed command's C..D region, head+tail with a marker when truncated), handled as bytes with invalid UTF-8 replaced, stripped of escape sequences before redaction, and redacted before it leaves the hook client. The session log itself is never transmitted whole and never leaves the machine.

A failure whose output is 5 MB of binary yields a context slice of at most 64 KB with a truncation marker, valid UTF-8, no escape sequences, and redacted tokens; a test asserts the log path never appears in the agent request.

No auto-apply in v1: every proposal, including package installs and container stops, waits for an explicit keypress; there is no 'safe auto-fix policy' switch yet, and 'sudo' proposals are shown with the exact command and never pre-typed into the prompt.

The fixture agent proposing 'sudo apt install x' shows the exact command and requires Enter; a proposal is never inserted into READLINE_LINE; no code path executes a proposal without the approval function returning true.

'nvsh doctor' gains in-shell checks with remediations: hook file sourced, nvsh hook first in PROMPT_COMMAND, Enter/Tab/Ctrl+G bindings present in the active keymap, capture active (script or tmux pipe-pane) with the log path and mode, daemon and pi status, harness reachable, terminfo present; '/doctor' prints the same inline.
'nvsh doctor' run inside a hooked shell reports each in-shell check with pass/fail and a remediation; run with the hook deliberately moved to last position it fails the ordering check.

Approval allowlists: 'approved for user' lives at $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/nvsh/approved.toml (0600) as glob patterns matched against the full command line with fnmatch semantics; 'approved for session' lives in the daemon's memory and dies with it. Defaults ship read-only inspectors ('nvidia-smi *', 'docker ps*', 'journalctl *', 'systemctl status *', 'df *', 'free *', 'nvsh *') and never 'sudo *', 'rm *' or a bare '*'; 'nvsh approve list/add/remove' and '/approve' manage them; every allowlisted execution is still written to the audit log.

A test drives the fixture agent through 'nvidia-smi -q' (runs without prompt via the default list), 'apt install foo' (prompts; 'approve for session' makes a second call run; a new daemon prompts again), and 'sudo rm -rf /x' (prompts even after 'approve for user' is attempted, because sudo and rm patterns are refused by the add command); the audit log holds all three.

Session daemon model (from decision on q9): one nvsh daemon and one pi process per user, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nvsh/daemon.sock; each shell session (keyed by the hook's shell PID) owns its own pi conversation. When a request arrives from a shell other than the active one, the daemon puts the active conversation to sleep (pi rpc switch_session / new_session, which persist to the nvsh-owned session dir) and activates the caller's conversation, resuming it on its next request. 'sessions.max' in config allows more concurrent pi processes for machines that can afford them.

With two terminals: a failure in A, then a failure in B, then '/ask what did you just see' in A answers about A's failure only; pgrep shows one pi process throughout; on orin (no node) the daemon reports 'pi unavailable' and the client falls back to the configured stdlib adapter.

CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.colleague.md, QWEN.md and .pi/SYSTEM.md all describe the hook architecture; the 'Login-shell constraints' section is replaced by 'Hook constraints'; 'uv run python scripts/harness-smoke.py --stage config --require config' passes

tasks.summary: Trigger rules module nvsh/triggers.py with table-driven tests
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_triggers.py is a table over (command, exit, pipestatus, pipefail, program_class, rate_state) with one row per rule in CLAUDE.md's trigger list plus ssh/docker exec/kubectl exec/tmux/screen/su/sudo -i pass-through; every non-error row yields decision 'skip' with a reason

130, 141, grep/diff exit 1, false, test/[ ], and a command run while the shell is inside a script produce 'skip'; 'ls /nope' exit 2 produces 'ask'; the rate limiter refuses a second auto call inside the configured window and records it
nvsh/triggers.py imports only stdlib and exposes decide(event) -> Decision with fields action, reason, rule_id
tasks.instruction: Pure functions, no I/O. Pipeline status: honour the shell's pipefail setting as given in the event; do not re-derive. Program class comes from the first word of the command (vim, htop, jtop, less, ssh, docker, kubectl, tmux, screen, su, sudo -i) — keep the list in one frozenset so t8 can reuse it for the hook.

tasks.summary: Redactor nvsh/redact.py with corpus tests
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_redact.py has a corpus file with HF_TOKEN=, --api-key, Authorization: Bearer, OPENAI_API_KEY=, .env-style KEY=value, ssh private-key blocks, and JSON 'apiKey' fields; every secret is replaced by a typed marker and no secret substring survives
redact(bytes) -> bytes handles invalid UTF-8 and escape sequences without raising; a property test asserts idempotence

tasks.summary: Platform detection nvsh/platform/ (file-first) plus docs/platforms.md
acceptance_criteria: detect() returns a Platform with kind in {dgx-spark, jetson, rtx, generic}, every value carrying (value, source_path_or_command); fixture trees for spark, thor and orin (copied from the real files) make the tests reproduce DGX Spark/DGX OS 7.x/CUDA 13.0.2/driver 580.126.09, AGX Thor/R38.2/cuDNN 9.12/TensorRT 10.13, AGX Orin/R39.2 with CUDA toolkit and tensorrt reported absent

nvidia-smi memory [N/A] is mapped to unified-memory mode and MemAvailable is reported as the pressure signal; nvpmodel, cuDNN, TensorRT, tmux, pi, spark (dgx-spark-cli) are reported present/absent, never omitted
docs/platforms.md lists every value, its source, whether it is a file read or subprocess, and the verifying command for spark, thor and orin
tasks.instruction: Prefer file reads (/etc/dgx-release, /etc/nv_tegra_release, /proc/device-tree/model and compatible, /sys/class/dmi/id/product_name, /usr/local/cuda/version.json, /proc/driver/nvidia/version, /proc/meminfo, /usr/include/aarch64-linux-gnu/cudnn_version.h, /etc/docker/daemon.json). Subprocess only for nvidia-smi, nvpmodel -q, dpkg-query, docker info, with timeouts. Call 'spark status --json' when on PATH and merge, never require it.

tasks.summary: Config and approval store: nvsh/config.py, nvsh/approvals.py
acceptance_criteria: config loads $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/nvsh/config.toml with tomllib, defaults to [agent] provider='pi' and [agents.pi] provider='nemotron' model='associate', sessions.max=1, and never reads or stores API keys; missing file yields defaults

approvals: approved.toml (0600) holds glob patterns; matches(cmd) uses fnmatch on the full command line; add() refuses 'sudo *', 'rm *', bare '*' and patterns starting with 'sudo'/'rm'; the default list contains 'nvidia-smi *', 'docker ps*', 'journalctl *', 'systemctl status *', 'df *', 'free *', 'nvsh *'; a session list lives in memory only
every example config under docs/ or nvsh/ uses http://localhost placeholders; scripts/scan-secrets.py passes
tasks.instruction: Two small modules, both stdlib. Expose Approvals.decide(cmd) -> 'user' | 'session' | 'ask' so t11's extension and t13's client share it via `nvsh approve check <cmd> --json`.

tasks.summary: Agent contract nvsh/agent/ with FakeAgent and conformance tests
acceptance_criteria: nvsh/agent/base.py defines NvshAgent (start, run -> iterator of events, cancel, close, capabilities), AgentRequest(kind failure|slash|explicit, prompt, command, exit_code, failure_id), AgentContext, events text_delta|tool_call|tool_result|proposal|status|done|error; nothing imports pi

FakeAgent replays a scripted event list; tests/test_agent_conformance.py runs the same suite (streaming order, cancel mid-stream, error propagation, capability report, teardown) against every registered adapter via a fixture

tests/test_approval_loop.py drives FakeAgent through inspect -> proposal 'sudo rm -rf /x' -> the proposal is rendered and never executed until approve() returns True -> retry -> verify; the audit log (jsonl) records proposal, decision, outcome; a proposal is never written into READLINE_LINE
tasks.instruction: Keep the loop (nvsh/agent/loop.py) UI-free: it takes an approve callback and an executor. The audit log path is $XDG_STATE_HOME/nvsh/audit.jsonl. This is the module every later task plugs into; keep the public surface tiny.

tasks.summary: Readline layer nvsh/shell/readline.bash: Enter macro, /+Tab palette, argument completion, Ctrl+G, all keymaps
acceptance_criteria: under script(1) with CR keystrokes, in emacs mode and after 'set -o vi': '/doctor' and '/ask why' route to ' nvsh slash `<line>`' and 'history' shows the original line only; '/notacmd', 'ls -d /tmp' and a quoted two-line echo pass through unchanged; Ctrl+G prints the panel hook and restores the line

'/'+Tab lists slash commands merged with real paths, '/do'+Tab completes /doctor, '/tm'+Tab completes /tmp/, '/doctor '+Tab lists its arguments from 'nvsh complete --json', 'ec'+Tab still lists echo; bash-completion's -D loader is untouched and complete -I is registered by nvsh
a deliberately erroring hook function still lets Enter accept the line (degrade, never lock)
tasks.instruction: Bind with 'bind -m emacs', 'bind -m vi-insert', 'bind -m vi-command'. Enter: bind -x on an unused sequence plus a C-m macro ending in C-j. Completion data comes only from 'nvsh complete' (t16); never duplicate the command list in bash. HISTCONTROL: append ignorespace if absent, and document it.

tasks.summary: Capture layer nvsh/capture.py: session log, OSC 133 slicing, tmux pipe-pane, bounding
acceptance_criteria: open_session_log() creates $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nvsh/`<shell-pid>`.log with mode 0600, refuses to start when already under script/tmux or when NVSH_WRAPPED is set, and removes the log at shell exit; killing script(1) mid-session is simulated and the reader returns 'no capture' without raising

last_slice(log) returns exactly the bytes between the last OSC 133 C and D markers (fixture from the scratchpad experiment: 'hello-out' + 'ls: cannot access'), capped at 64 KB with head+tail and a truncation marker, escape sequences stripped, invalid UTF-8 replaced; the log path never appears in the returned context
inside tmux ($TMUX set) the source is 'tmux pipe-pane -o' to the same log; a test proves only the slice, never the whole log, reaches the redactor
tasks.instruction: The wrapper command rendered for the hook is: exec script -qfc "$BASH" "$log" with NVSH_WRAPPED=1 exported. Bound first, then strip, then redact (t3). Provide 'nvsh capture --show' for --show-context.

tasks.summary: PiAgent nvsh/agent/pi.py: rpc subprocess, launch hygiene, abort
acceptance_criteria: PiAgent builds argv 'pi --mode rpc --no-context-files --no-extensions --no-skills --no-prompt-templates --no-approve --session-dir $XDG_STATE_HOME/nvsh/pi-sessions -e `<approval extension path>`' (asserted in a test); the reader splits on LF only and tolerates U+2028; message_update text deltas, tool_execution_* and extension_ui_request map to NvshAgent events

cancel() sends {type: abort} and returns within 1 s; a killed pi process yields an error event and never hangs the caller; after a run no file appears under ~/.pi/agent/sessions (test uses HOME in tmp)
the conformance suite from t6 passes against PiAgent using a fake 'pi' script on PATH that speaks the rpc protocol from docs/rpc.md
tasks.instruction: subprocess.Popen with pipes, a reader thread and a queue; no asyncio. Ship the fake pi as tests/fakes/pi so CI never needs node. Capabilities: streaming, toolCalling, cancellation, persistentSession, localModel true.

tasks.summary: Harness chooser and adapters: nvsh/agent/registry.py, openai_compat.py, claude.py, codex.py, qwen.py
acceptance_criteria: 'nvsh agent list --json' reports pi, qwen, claude, codex, openai-compat with installed status from PATH; 'nvsh agent use `<name>`' writes config; with none installed the failure panel text offers 'install pi' or 'choose another harness'

OpenAICompatAgent uses stdlib urllib against an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint with streaming, 5 s connect timeout, bearer from an env var name in config (never a literal), and passes the conformance suite against a local fake HTTP server

claude ('claude -p --output-format stream-json'), codex ('codex exec --json') and qwen ('qwen -p') adapters are thin subprocess mappers with capability declarations and pass the conformance suite via fake scripts on PATH; 'nvsh setup' on a host without node (orin) selects openai-compat and prints why
tasks.instruction: Registry is a dict of factories like culture_core/cli/agents.py:788. Do not add dependencies. The install offer for pi runs 'npm install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent' only after a keypress and only when npm exists.

tasks.summary: pi approval extension nvsh/agent/pi_ext/approval.ts with user/session allowlists
acceptance_criteria: the extension registers a tool_call handler: for the bash tool it runs 'nvsh approve check `<cmd>` --json'; 'user' or 'session' allows, 'ask' raises extension_ui_request with choices once/session/user; a blocked call returns {block: true, reason}; non-bash tools are blocked in v1

a Node-free test parses the .ts for the required handlers; a live test (skipped when pi is absent) drives the fake-agent script from t6 through nvidia-smi (runs), 'apt install foo' (asks; approve-for-session then runs; new daemon asks again) and 'sudo rm -rf /x' (asks even after approve-for-user is attempted) with all three in the audit log
the .ts file ships inside the wheel (hatch include) and is referenced by absolute path from PiAgent
tasks.instruction: Keep the TypeScript under 120 lines and dependency-free (pi's ExtensionAPI only, per docs/extensions.md:1338-1387 and 751-793). All policy lives in Python (t5); the extension only forwards.

tasks.summary: Session daemon nvsh/daemon.py: per-user socket, per-shell conversations, sleep/switch, fallback
acceptance_criteria: starting a shell creates no nvsh or pi process; the first qualifying failure starts one daemon on $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nvsh/daemon.sock (0600) and one agent process; closing the last shell (EXIT trap) or an idle timeout stops both (pgrep-based test)

two simulated shells A and B: failure in A, failure in B, then '/ask what did you just see' from A answers from A's conversation only; one pi process throughout; conversations sleep via switch_session/new_session and resume on the shell's next request; sessions.max=2 allows a second process
with the daemon missing or crashed the client falls back to a one-shot adapter run; with pi absent the daemon reports 'pi unavailable' and uses the configured fallback adapter
tasks.instruction: socketserver.ThreadingUnixStreamServer, JSON lines, stdlib only. Protocol: {shell, kind, request} -> stream of events. Keep the daemon runnable in the foreground for tests. Reap stale sockets at start.

tasks.summary: Failure client and panel nvsh/client.py + nvsh/panel.py: context assembly, streaming, approve keys, retry, verify, Ctrl+C
acceptance_criteria: the client assembles AgentContext from the hook args, the redacted output slice, and the platform block (every value with its source); 'nvsh context --show' prints exactly the bytes that would be sent; a test with sockets disabled proves a localhost endpoint is still reached (air-gapped mode)

Ctrl+C while streaming aborts the agent run, restores the terminal and returns to a working prompt within 1 s; '/fix' afterwards still finds the last failure (state file under $XDG_STATE_HOME/nvsh/last-failure.json); retry re-runs only after Enter and verify reports the new exit status

tasks.instruction: Pure bash 5.1+, every function ends with '|| return 0', never set -e. Prepend with PROMPT_COMMAND=(__nvsh_hook plus the existing elements), handling the string form. tasks.summary: Setup, uninstall, on/off verbs: nvsh/cli/_commands/setup.py and the rc editor nvsh/rcfile.py; wheel includes

the rendered hook file carries the nvsh version; a client run with an older stamp prints the refresh notice once per session; nvsh uninstall removes the block (restoring the backup if the block was edited), hook files, sockets, logs and daemons and leaves the rc byte-identical to the backup; nvsh off and nvsh on unbind and rebind in the current shell
the wheel built from a clean checkout contains nvsh/shell/*.bash and nvsh/agent/pi_ext/*.ts (hatch include) and nvsh setup works from a clean venv install; dependencies stays empty
tasks.instruction: Render hook files from package resources (importlib.resources) into the user's data dir. Every verb: register(sub), CliError, emit_result, --json, catalog entry. Also add the thin 'nvsh hook' verb the bash hook calls on failure (parse args, hand to t13's client).

orin has no node: pi cannot be installed there without also installing node; t11's openai-compat fallback is the v1 answer, install-node is a follow-up.
